verdict: Caution: lend selectively to tier-2 component makers with diversified OEM books and tight monthly monitoring; avoid single-OEM, EV-exposed engine-part units and any proposal without verified GST and power data.
title: Rudrapur Auto & Auto Components: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What this business physically is
**Rudrapur's auto cluster sits inside SIDCUL, and local reporting says the auto and electronics sectors there have picked up momentum [1].** A component unit here takes steel, aluminium and polymer, stamps or moulds or machines it to an OEM's drawing, and ships on a schedule to an assembly line. Cash turns on the OEM's payment cycle, not on the unit's own sales effort. **The value sits in the tooling and the approved-vendor status, not in the machines** — which is why a supplier with a live part number and a two-year-old relationship is a different credit from one chasing its first order.

## Where cash and risk sit now
**The national demand picture is strong: IIP for NIC 29 output is +25.2% YoY and +19.2% Apr-to-date [D].** Peer results agree — Motherson Sumi Wiring's Q2 revenue grew 46.7% to Rs 4,054 crore with profit up 35% to Rs 223 crore [4], and Lumax lifted its growth target after a strong first half [7]. **But the local economy is not keeping pace: Uttarakhand GST collections are -19.1% Apr-to-date against India's +6.1%, and state electricity demand is +4.7% against India's +9.5% [D].** So when a proposal lands, check the unit's own GST turnover trend against the state number; if the unit's filings are flat while the state is down 19.1%, ask what is holding it up — a genuine new part number, or receivables being stretched.

**Margin is the second pressure point.** ASK Automotive posted record revenue but aluminium squeezed margins [5], and Elara expects Q4FY26 auto EBITDA growth of about 21% with commodity risk rising [6]. **Component makers rarely pass metal cost through immediately, so a unit with no price-escalation clause absorbs the squeeze.** Ask for the clause; if there is none, size the facility to absorb one quarter of metal inflation.

## Who to pursue, who to avoid
**Pursue tier-2 suppliers with two or more OEM customers, a mix of ICE and non-engine parts, and job-work or tooling revenue alongside production.** ICRA notes that engine and engine-related parts carry higher obsolescence risk as EVs spread, while complex fuel-injection work carries real pricing power [11]. **Avoid single-OEM units, pure engine-part specialists, and anyone whose entire order book is one platform.** Also avoid units with large debt-funded capex: rating criteria flag Debt/EBITDA above 2.5-2.75 times as a red line [10].

## How to grow safely
**Structure as a cash-flow loan against verified receivables, not a clean term loan.** Take monthly GST returns, e-way bills, and the OEM's payment statement. **Take stock and debtor statements every month, and a quarterly CMA.** Note that gross current assets in this sector have averaged 160-170 days [10] — so if a unit claims a 90-day cycle, ask for the debtor ageing to prove it.

## Early warning signs
**Watch for GST turnover falling faster than the state's -19.1% [D], electricity bill arrears, and a shift from OEM billing to job-work billing.** A factory accident, like the July fatality reported at a Rudrapur auto factory [3], can halt a line and delay dispatches — check safety records. **If the OEM's own volumes soften, the tier-2 supplier feels it within one quarter.**

arrears or disconnection notice -> stop disbursement, inspect plant
receivable days stretch beyond 90 -> reprice or reduce limit
inventory days rise above 60 -> ask for slow-moving stock list
crosses 2.5x -> move to watchlist, seek promoter infusion
